title: Ulyana and the Spire
premise: Ada Montrose, a cartographer who maps realms that shouldn't exist, inherits a dying stranger's map of the Spire — the anchor point where the covenant between the human world and the unmapped realms was sealed centuries ago. The map reveals that her own guild has been siphoning the covenant's power for generations, trading in 'impossible things' harvested from a slowly dying otherworld, and that her grandmother was the last keeper who tried to stop it. Pursued by guild enforcers and guided by the stranger's ghost-memory embedded in the map, Ada must reach the Spire and reforge the covenant before it collapses entirely. In the end she chooses to break her family's inheritance rather than claim it, sacrificing her own memories of the unmapped realms to seal a new, equal covenant — and wakes with blank ledgers and an ache she cannot name.
about_author: Wendell Sandoval is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing antique maps before turning to fiction full-time. He writes from a coastal town where the fog rolls in early, and claims his best ideas arrive on days he can't see the horizon.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Ada Montrose audits the Cartographers' Guild's ledgers, noticing entries for goods that cannot exist — bottled starlight, a river's first word. Her POV establishes her precision, loneliness, and quiet suspicion of the guild's masters. When she questions a senior cartographer, she's warned off with unusual menace. Emotional beat: unease taking root beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Inkwell Door
chapters.summary: A gaunt, half-dead man collapses into Ada's mapping room, pressing a folded map into her hands and gasping that 'the Spire remembers her name.' Guild enforcers arrive moments later; the stranger dies buying Ada time to flee through the guild's back ways. His POV briefly opens the chapter, revealing he chose her deliberately. Emotional beat: terror and the vertigo of being chosen.

chapters.title: What the Map Remembers
chapters.summary: Hiding in the old canal district, Ada studies the map and discovers it responds to her touch, unfurling paths no ink should hold. The dead stranger's voice — a memory called Emeric — speaks from its lines, explaining the covenant between realms and naming her grandmother as the last keeper. Emotional beat: grief braided with wonder as family history rewrites itself.

chapters.title: The Guild's Long Theft
chapters.summary: Emeric shows Ada the truth: every 'impossible thing' in the ledgers was carved from the otherworld's living substance, and the Spire — the covenant's anchor — is failing because of it. Ada realizes her employers are thieves on a generational scale. Enforcers close in; she barely escapes with the map. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Crossing the Unmapped Border
chapters.summary: Ada uses her cartographer's craft to walk a border only she can read, slipping into the otherworld: a realm of fading colors and starving magic. She meets the Vessels, diminished beings who once kept the covenant, who test her intentions and reveal what her grandmother sacrificed. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by guilt over her guild's crimes.

chapters.title: Her Grandmother's Hand
chapters.summary: In a ruined waystation, Ada finds her grandmother's hidden journal, learning the old keeper tried to reforge the covenant and was betrayed by her own guild — by Ada's mother. The journal holds half the ritual needed at the Spire, but warns the reforge demands a price from the one who performs it. Emotional beat: inherited wounds opened anew.

chapters.title: The Hunt Through Hollow Light
chapters.summary: Guild master Corvane himself crosses into the otherworld with enforcers, determined to seize the map and let the Spire fall so the guild can harvest what remains unchecked. A chase through dissolving landscapes costs Ada allies among the Vessels. Emeric's memory begins fraying, his voice thinning. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Ascent of the Spire
chapters.summary: Ada reaches the Spire — a tower grown from covenant-law itself, its stones cracked and weeping light. Climbing it, she relives the covenant's making through Emeric's fading memories and confronts how power was hoarded from the very start. Corvane arrives below, offering her inheritance of the guild if she walks away. Emotional beat: temptation weighed against conscience.

chapters.title: Reforge or Ruin
chapters.summary: At the summit, Ada begins the rite as Corvane's forces storm the Spire. The covenant demands a price: she offers not gold or blood but her memories of the unmapped realms — everything Emeric showed her, her grandmother's face in the journal, the wonder itself. The new covenant seals as the old order shatters; Corvane is unmade by the law he exploited. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into triumph.

chapters.title: Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Ada wakes in her mapping room, ledgers empty, the guild dissolved, the world subtly brighter though she doesn't know why. On her desk lies a blank map and a note in a hand like her grandmother's: 'Some inheritances are meant to be ended.' She picks up her pen and begins drawing something new. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace, and the courage to begin again.
